provenance.instrument: Robinson Township Zoning Ordinance (Chapter 300 Zoning, Ord. No. 3-1993, amended in its entirety 6-5-2017 by Res. No. 8-2017, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 RO0250 (Township of Robinson, Allegheny County: Board of Commissioners, appeals to the Allegheny County Court of Common Pleas, 300-27M(3)). 'Includes legislation through 04-01-2024'. The New Laws list on the chapter shows four uncodified zoning amendments: Ord. No. 2-2025 and 3-2025 (3-3-2025), 4-2025 (7-7-2025) and 2-2026 (5-4-2026). All four PDFs were read in full on 2026-11-26.
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360: 'Includes legislation through 04-01-2024'. New Laws: Ord. No. 2-2025, 3-2025, 4-2025 and 2-2026, each 'Zoning Amendment' to Chapter 300, not codified.
provenance.code_caution: Four zoning amendments are not yet in the online code. Their PDFs were read in full on 2026-11-26. Ord. No. 2-2026 (5-4-2026) amends 300-36 R-1: single-family lots 17,500 sq ft (was 25,000), 100 ft wide (was 150), front yard 35 ft (was 75); all other R-1 provisions stay. The file uses these figures. Ord. No. 2-2025 (3-3-2025) amends 300-39 R-4: townhouses 2,200 sq ft of lot area per unit, multi-family lots 100 ft wide, coverage 50% for townhouses and multi-family and 40% for other uses, front yards 45 ft from the curb on a public street and 30 ft on a private street, townhouse and garden apartment side yards 10 ft, townhouse rear 20 ft, building spacing 20 ft. Ord. No. 3-2025 (3-3-2025) creates the High-Density Multiple-Family Low-Rise Apartment Dwelling Overlay District on land in C-3, for low-rise apartments (1,700 sq ft of lot area per unit, four stories and 60 ft, R-4 rules otherwise). Ord. No. 4-2025 (7-7-2025) lowers the R-3 side yard for 'All other principal uses' from 20 to 10 ft. The single-family side yard of 7 ft is unchanged. None of the four names an accessory or second dwelling unit.
checks: The zoning code has no accessory dwelling unit, in-law suite or similar listing. 'No accessory structure shall be used for dwelling purposes' (300-73D(2)), so a unit in a garage or other accessory building is barred

A single-family dwelling is 'a detached residential building, other than a mobile home, designed for or occupied exclusively by one family, which is the only principal structure on the lot and is permanently attached to a foundation' (300-12). A second unit inside the house makes it a two-family or multiple-family dwelling

Two-family dwellings are permitted by right in R-3 (10,000 sq ft) and R-5 (14,000 sq ft), and new ones in the Mobility Overlay Districts MOD-A, MOD-B and MOD-C. R-4, C-2, C-3, C-4 and MOD-D permit only existing two-family dwellings

Conversion of an existing single-family dwelling into a multiple-family dwelling (three or more units) is a special exception in R-3 and a permitted use in R-4. Each unit at least 800 sq ft with a kitchen and bath, two parking spaces per unit (300-103A(4))
A single-family dwelling may also take up to two unrelated boarders, one parking space each, or foster persons placed by court order (300-66)

Accessory structures are 20 ft in the residential districts, not in the required front yard, at the principal side yard (300-73C(2)), and at most 30% of the required rear yard. The rear yard for accessory uses is 10 ft in general (300-73C(3)) and by district: R-1 10 ft, R-2, R-3 and R-5 6 ft, R-4 50 ft, MOD-A to MOD-C 6 ft, MOD-D 50 ft. On corner lots accessory side yards are R-1 8 ft, R-2 6 ft, R-3 5 ft
In any residential district single- and two-family dwellings may be up to 10 ft taller than the district height, to at most 45 ft, with side and rear yards each 10 ft larger (300-35A)

C-4 and C-5 allow temporary living quarters for a caretaker, watchman or security personnel (300-73A(16)), and in C-4 and I-1 a guard or custodian may reside on the premises. These are not homes on a house lot

Mobility Overlay Districts supersede the base district (300-50). Airport Hazard and Parkway Protection Overlays add rules. Ord. No. 3-2025 adds a High-Density Multiple-Family Low-Rise Apartment Dwelling Overlay District on land in C-3
provenance.notes: Fix round after independent review, 2026-11-15: R-1 lot and front yard from Ord. No. 2-2026 (search excerpts), the four amendments described in code_caution, accessory rear and side yards by district, the 150 ft overlay lot width and 300-35A added. Zoning office: Robinson Township Zoning Officer. Read in a browser on eCode360, one page at a time, on 2026-11-15. Searched the code (scope all) for accessory apartment, accessory dwelling, in-law, ECHO, elder cottage, granny, relative, housekeeping unit, caretaker, guest house, tenant house, living quarters, sleeping quarters, immediate family, watchman, separate living, cooking facilities, tiny house, caregiver, second dwelling and non-family, then for two-family, duplex, conversion, converted, manufactured home, mobile home, farm dwelling, age-restricted, agricultural employ, family dwelling and one principal, then for not listed, not specifically, unlisted, dictionary and mobility overlay. Read in full: 300-11, 300-27, Article IV (300-31 to 300-49), 300-50 to 300-52, 300-64, 300-73, 300-103A(4). Read on screen: the 300-12 definitions named in the notes and the 300-79E parking schedule. 300-11 has no rule for undefined words ('The particular shall control the general'). No unlisted-use clause and no bar on use variances was found. 300-64D speaks of 'the farm residence' only. Not read: Article VI, 300-98, 300-105, the rest of Articles VII to XIII, the New Laws PDFs and the attachments Second review, 2026-11-26: the four New Laws PDFs (Ord. No. 2-2025, 3-2025, 4-2025, 2-2026) read in full; the R-1 lot and front yard now rest on Ord. No. 2-2026 itself, and its Section 5 keeps the other R-1 figures. Article VI (300-53 and on, planned residential developments) read: a PRD permits single-family, two-family, townhouse and multiple-family dwellings and residential accessory uses (300-53B), no accessory or second unit with a house. Left for a later check, neither changes the ADU answer: whether R-3's 'Conversion (single-family to a multiple-family dwelling): 1,200 square feet' (300-38C(1)(e)) is lot area per unit (the neighbouring rows say 'per dwelling unit', this one does not), and the lot answer shows base district yards where a Mobility Overlay supersedes them (said as a condition).

path.note: A second dwelling unit with a single-family dwelling is not a listed use. It needs a use variance from the Zoning Hearing Board (MPC 910.2). No section read bars a use variance. In R-3 and R-5 a two-family dwelling is permitted by right, and in R-3 a conversion to three or more units is a special exception

value.name: Two-family dwelling
value.conditions: A new two-family dwelling is permitted by right in R-3 (10,000 sq ft, 55 ft wide, side yards 10 ft) and R-5 (14,000 sq ft, 75 ft wide). It is 'a detached residential building containing separate, independent dwelling units for two families, with the units attached either side by side or one over the other, which is the only principal structure on the lot'. Two parking spaces per dwelling unit (300-79E). Only existing two-family dwellings are permitted in R-4, C-2, C-3, C-4 and MOD-D
value.note: Not an ADU listing. A building type. Whether a single-family house may be altered into a two-family dwelling is not stated

value.name: Two-family dwelling in a Mobility Overlay District
value.conditions: 'Two-family dwelling, new' is a permitted use in MOD-A, MOD-B and MOD-C, which supersede the base district (300-50). Lot area per the R-3 District (10,000 sq ft for a two-family dwelling). Lot width at least 150 ft: MOD-A 'Residential uses not including live-work units: 150 feet', MOD-B and MOD-C 'All other residential uses: 150 feet'. Side yards 10 ft in MOD-A and MOD-C, 40 ft in MOD-B. Two parking spaces per dwelling unit

requires.condition: The lot is at least 150 ft wide (residential uses other than live-work units in MOD-A, all other residential uses in MOD-B and MOD-C)

value.note: Not an ADU listing. A building type, only where an overlay is mapped

value.name: Conversion of an existing single-family dwelling to a multiple-family dwelling
value.conditions: A special exception in R-3 (300-38B(3)(d)) and a permitted use in R-4 (300-39B(1)(e)). A multiple-family dwelling has 'three or more separate independent dwelling units'. Each unit at least 800 sq ft with a kitchen and bath, two parking spaces per unit in a paved rear-yard area, a buffer or six-foot opaque fence (300-103A(4)). R-3 lists 'Conversion (single-family to a multiple-family dwelling): 1,200 square feet' and 50 ft width
value.note: Not an ADU listing. Three or more units in all. In R-4 it is a permitted use. Whether R-3's 1,200 sq ft is per unit or for the lot is not stated

value.condition: In the Mobility Overlay Districts the overlay's use list and figures supersede the base district (300-50). MOD-A, MOD-B and MOD-C permit new two-family dwellings, MOD-D only existing single-family and two-family dwellings. Single-family figures: MOD-A 5,000 sq ft, front 25 ft, side 10 ft, rear 25 ft, 45 ft. MOD-B the R-3 lot figures, 80 ft wide, front 40 ft, side 15 ft, rear 35 ft. MOD-C 5,000 sq ft, 80 ft wide, front 25 ft, side 10 ft, rear 35 ft. MOD-D 5,000 sq ft, front 75 ft, side 50 ft, rear 50 ft. Accessory uses stand 6 ft from the rear line in MOD-A, MOD-B and MOD-C and 50 ft in MOD-D.
In the Parkway Protection Overlay buildings stand at least twice their height and at least 100 ft from the parkway right-of-way (less on shallow lots, never under 25 ft).
